The requirement of s.304-8 is that the death of a woman be caused by burns, bodily injury or otherwise than in normal circumstances, within seven years of her marriage. Further, it should be shown that soon before her death, she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or her husband's family or relatives and thirdly, that such harassment should be in relation to a demand for dowry
The trial court held all the three accused guilty under Section 304-B IPC and sentenced them to undergo life imprisonment. The High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence.

neutral_facts.value: The accused, who were the husband, brother-in-law, and mother-in-law of the deceased woman, were found guilty of her death after pouring kerosene on her. The deceased died an unnatural death within seven years of her marriage. There was persistent demand for dowry items like a refrigerator, television, and cooler, which led to her being subjected to cruelty and ill-treatment. The deceased was found dead in her matrimonial home, and the body was handed over to her family. The accused were found to have absconded after the body was handed over. The prosecution presented evidence including witness statements, medical reports, and physical evidence from the scene, which indicated that the deceased was set on fire. The accused were found to have injuries consistent with struggling or fighting, and there was no evidence of cooking materials in the kitchen, which contradicted their claim of an accidental death. The trial court convicted all three accused under Section 304-B IPC, and the High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Court applied the legal principle that the death of a woman caused by burns, bodily injury or otherwise than in normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his family, in relation to a demand for dowry, is considered a 'dowry death' and the husband or relative is presumed to have caused her death.

quotes.text: The requirement of Section 304-B is that the death of a woman be caused by burns, bodily injury or otherwise than in normal circumstances, within seven years of her marriage.
